html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. PHI: protected health information; BAA: business associate agreement; FedRAMP: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program; DPA: data processing addendum; MCP: Model Context Protocol; RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation; GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation; HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act

  • A time plan for 63 items in 120 minutes
  • A method to read an item, find the binding constraint and eliminate distractors
  • How to handle multiple-response items
  • Policies and logistics on exam day
  • A final review checklist and a plan for the last week

2Time Plan

  • 63 items in 120 minutes is about 1 minute 54 seconds per item; scenario items are longer, so pace yourself.
  • First pass (about 85 minutes): answer what you know in about 80 seconds, mark the rest.
  • Second pass (about 25 minutes): work the marked items.
  • Last 10 minutes: check multiple-response counts and blanks.
  • Never leave an item blank. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item in the first pass.
  • Only the total scaled score (720) decides pass or fail.
Exam tip

Architect items are scenario-heavy. Read for the constraint and the symptom; the stem usually contains the clue that rules out most options.

3Reading an Item

  1. Read the last sentence first ("which change best...", "what is the most likely first place to investigate?") and note how many answers.
  2. Find the binding constraint in the stem: latency, cost, security, compliance, accuracy, maintainability, scale.
  3. Predict the answer before reading the options.
  4. Compare options with the ten decision rules (Module 0) and the chooser (Module 18).
Word in the stem Points to...
"least privilege", "role only needs" Remove the capability
"same prompt every request", "latency and cost" Cache the stable prefix, static first
"after a document refresh", "confident but wrong" Retrieval and indexing
"exact identifiers", "clause numbers" Keyword / hybrid retrieval
"totals", "aggregations", "table" Structured query, not vector search
"hundreds of tools", "tool selection errors" Tool search / progressive discovery
"steps known in advance" Workflow
"path depends on discoveries", "unpredictable subtasks" Orchestrator-workers or agent
"independent branches, beyond one context" Multi-agent (cost aware)
"who is the user", "shared account" Per-user identity and authorization in code
"PHI" / "federal" / "EU personal data" BAA and eligible features / FedRAMP route / DPA, minimization, residency
"before releasing a change" Offline eval, A/B or canary, baseline
"irreversible", "regulated decision" Human approval gate
"client wants a guarantee" Honest, measurable SLA
"team cannot override" Managed settings
Exam tip

The correct option usually removes the cause (least privilege, retrieval fix, caching) instead of adding a detective control or a bigger model.

4Eliminating Distractors

Cross out options that:

  • Add logging, confirmation or monitoring where the real fix is removal or prevention
  • Rely on a stronger prompt or a bigger model for a design or security problem
  • Use an agent or multi-agent design for a fixed task
  • Truncate needed context or shrink the model without evidence
  • Use vector search for exact or aggregate queries
  • Skip evaluation or judge by anecdote
  • Use shared credentials, secrets client-side or tokens in URLs
  • Promise absolutes (100 percent accuracy, zero risk)
  • Assume compliance without contract, feature eligibility or route
Exam tip

Change an answer only when you can name the rule it breaks.

Multiple-response items

  • Choose exactly the stated number; judge each option on its own merits.
  • Eliminate clearly wrong options first; pairs are often two independent good practices (for example a control and a measure).

5Policies and Logistics

Topic What to know
Registration Through the Anthropic Partner Academy and Pearson VUE; online proctored or test center
Reschedule or cancel Up to 24 hours before; later changes forfeit the fee
ID Valid, unexpired government photo ID; the name must match the registration exactly
Accommodations Request and get approval from Pearson VUE before scheduling
Agreements You accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement; never share exam content
Conduct Stay in view of the webcam if online; clear desk; no phones, watches, headphones or notes
Retakes 14 / 30 / 90 days; max 4 attempts per rolling 12 months; fee per attempt
Result Pass or fail and scaled score, plus percent correct per domain
Validity and renewal 12 months; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment; a lapsed credential needs the full exam
Appeals Within 14 days through Pearson VUE support; scoring standard and items are not appealable

[Verify live] The guide is version 1.0 (July 2026). Check the Partner Academy for the current guide, fee and rules before you book.

6Final Review Checklist

  • I can state the ten decision rules and name the right pattern for a problem shape.
  • I can justify a model tier with evals and name the levers for cost and latency.
  • I know caching rules and what breaks them.
  • I can audit for capability bloat and choose tool search or code execution with MCP.
  • I can find authorization gaps and explain MCP OAuth (audience, no passthrough, step-up).
  • I can design a RAG pipeline (chunking, hybrid index, contextual retrieval, rerank, freshness) and say when not to.
  • I can match retrieval to data shape and explain accuracy-latency trade-offs.
  • I can define metrics and datasets, grade with mixed methods and run A/B tests.
  • I can diagnose by layer and optimize cost per successful task.
  • I can design layered guardrails and human oversight.
  • I can map GDPR, HIPAA and FedRAMP to platform and contract choices, and test for bias.
  • I can run discovery, communicate trade-offs, set honest SLAs, and plan documentation and lifecycle.
  • I can configure Claude Code for a team with managed settings, CLAUDE.md, hooks and telemetry.
  • I have built one end-to-end solution with RAG, evaluation and observability.

The last week

  • Seven to four days before: reread the notes of Integration, Solution Design and Evaluation, redo their scenario questions, and write down every miss with the reason.
  • Three days before: walk through the decision chooser (Module 18) aloud; reread the names and values table.
  • The day before: light review only: the ten decision rules and the time plan. Check your ID, registration name and test setup, and sleep.
  • On the day: arrive or log in early, read each item's last sentence first, and keep to the time plan.
